A clean result above does **not** cover the following. Confirm each one manually before claiming conformance.

| Criterion | Why not automated | How to verify |

| 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) | 9 component(s) colour slotted text through the <slot> element (p-button-pure, p-drilldown-link, p-link-pure, p-text, p-heading). Computed style on the host reports a different colour, so contrast results for this text — including axe-core's — may be wrong in either direction. | Sample this text with a colour picker or the browser contrast inspector. |
| 2.1.1 Keyboard (operability) | tabindex="-1" is a legitimate pattern (roving tabindex, redundant links, programmatic focus targets), so it cannot be treated as a defect. | Operate each control with Enter, Space and arrow keys. |

## How This Audit Was Conducted
1. Automated axe-core baseline (Phase 1) for each URL in light and in dark (`axe`, `tree`, `coverage`).
2. Domain skill code review (Phases 2–7 and 9). Phase 8 was skipped because no data tables were present.
3. Behavioral Playwright (Phase 10) for keyboard and viewports 320 and 1024, again per URL and color scheme. Axe was not run again.

## Scope and Coverage
| Check | Ran? | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Code review | yes | Phases 2–7 and 9. Phase 8 skipped (no tables). |
| axe-core runtime | yes | Four scans: `/en/` and `/en/products/`, light and dark. Contrast and ARIA verdicts come from here. Passes were not retained in `raw/`. |
| Behavioural (focus order, traps, reflow, targets, tree) | yes | Keyboard and viewports 320 and 1024, both themes. Tree ran in Phase 1. |
| Authenticated routes | no | These pages are public. |

No prior audit run existed, so there is no baseline comparison.

The products keyboard pass recorded 100 tab stops, which is the scanner's default cap, so controls after that stop were not traversed. The home page recorded 55 tab stops and no keyboard trap. Closed menus, flyouts, and the search dialog were not opened before measurement, so their internal focus order was not scanned.

## Serious Issues

### 1. Catalog search status and results update without a live region
- **Severity:** serious
- **Source:** agent-review
- **Phase:** 6
- **WCAG:** 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA)
- **Impact:** Screen reader users are not told when the search prompt, loading state, or results change.
- **Location:** `ui-testing/app/components/header/GlobalHeaderProductSearch.tsx` on `http://localhost:3010/en/` and `http://localhost:3010/en/products/`
- **Confidence:** medium
- **Help URL:** https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html
- **Effort:** Medium — **Auto-fixable:** no — **Owner:** dev

The header search modal swaps prompt, loading, empty, and result text inside a plain container. The catalog result count on the products page already uses `aria-live="polite"`; this modal does not.

```tsx
<div aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" className="min-h-[120px]">
  {/* existing prompt, loading, empty, and result markup */}
</div>
```

- **Verify by:** Open search, type a query, and confirm a screen reader announces the status or result count without moving focus.

### 2. Client-side route changes do not move focus to the new page heading
- **Severity:** serious
- **Source:** agent-review
- **Phase:** 3
- **WCAG:** 2.4.3 Focus Order (A)
- **Impact:** Keyboard and screen reader users stay on the control that started navigation instead of the new page.
- **Location:** `ui-testing/app/[locale]/layout.tsx` on both audited URLs
- **Confidence:** medium
- **Help URL:** https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order.html
- **Effort:** Medium — **Auto-fixable:** no — **Owner:** dev

The skip link focuses `#page-heading`. Nothing moves focus there after a Next.js client navigation. The locale layout renders the page without a route-change focus effect.

```tsx
"use client";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";

export function RouteFocus() {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  useEffect(() => {
    const heading = document.getElementById("page-heading");
    if (!heading) return;
    heading.setAttribute("tabindex", "-1");
    heading.focus();
  }, [pathname]);
  return null;
}
```

- **Verify by:** Tab to a link that changes the route, activate it, and confirm focus is on the new page heading.

### 3. Horizontal scrolling required at 320px on the home page
- **Severity:** serious
- **Source:** playwright
- **Phase:** 10
- **WCAG:** 1.4.10 Reflow (AA)
- **Impact:** Users who zoom or use small screens must scroll in two dimensions.
- **Location:** `document` on `http://localhost:3010/en/`
- **Confidence:** high
- **Help URL:** https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html
- **Effort:** High — **Auto-fixable:** no — **Owner:** design

At 320px the home page scroll width was 336px against a 320px client width, in both light and dark. At 1024px it did not overflow. The products page did not overflow at either width.

- **Verify by:** Re-run `a11y-scan.mjs --mode viewport --viewports 320,1024` on `/en/` and confirm `reflowFailures` is empty.

## Cross-Page Patterns

The search live region and the route-change focus gap are template-level: both pages share `GlobalHeaderProductSearch` and the locale layout. One fix in each file covers both URLs.

Horizontal overflow is page-specific to the home page.

Both pages expose a banner, a navigation landmark named Main, a main landmark, a contentinfo footer, a skip link, and one `h1`. No keyboard trap was recorded on either page. Tab-stop counts differ sharply (55 on the home page, 100 on products, at the traversal cap), which matches the longer product grid rather than a second trap.

## What Passed

- axe-core reported no violations and no incomplete results on either URL in light or dark.
- Each page has `lang="en"`, a unique document title, one `h1`, a skip link, and the primary landmarks.
- Product and hero images in the accessibility tree have descriptive names. Decorative tile images use empty alt text.
- Feedback, sort, and search fields that are on these routes have visible labels. The products result count is in a polite live region.
- No ambiguous link names from the closed list were present.
- No undersized targets remained after the inline and spacing exceptions at 320px or 1024px.
- The products page reflowed without horizontal scrolling at both widths.

## Recommended Testing Setup

Automated checks cover a minority of WCAG. After the fixes, repeat the same scanner commands, then test manually:

- VoiceOver (macOS): rotor by headings and links; open search and listen for the result announcement; follow a client navigation and confirm the new heading is announced.
- Keyboard only: Tab from the skip link through header, main, and footer. Open the search modal and the filter flyout and leave them with Escape. Confirm focus returns to the control that opened them.
- Colour picker on slotted PDS text (`p-text`, `p-heading`, `p-link-pure`, `p-button-pure`, `p-drilldown-link`) in light and dark.
- Visible focus: Tab through PDS controls and confirm the focus ring is visible in both themes.

## Next Steps

1. Add a polite live region around header search status.
2. Move focus to `#page-heading` after client navigations.
3. Remove the horizontal overflow on the home page at 320px (scroll width 336px, client width 320px).
4. Confirm slotted-text contrast and focus rings by hand.
5. Optional follow-ups: apply fixes, export CSV / SARIF / HTML, or compare a later run against this `findings.json`.

## Known Limitations

This is not a WCAG conformance claim. Shadow DOM is traversed, but component-internal state (open menus, search results, filter flyout, focus inside closed overlays) is only checked where it is reachable by Tab on the loaded page. The products keyboard traversal stopped at the 100-tab cap. Slotted-text contrast can be wrong in either direction for axe-core and for any computed-style check. Focus-indicator visibility was not measured.
